title: Install matching kernel headers before broadcom-wl-dkms
head: 40fc412e5e7f
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: The new shell test fails against the current base-tip package helpers
leads.consequence: At the current quattro tip, omarchy-pkg-present calls pacman -Q -- <pkg>, but the test's fake pacman treats $2 (--) as the package name. Its fake -S would also append -- to the installed-package list. In the actual base-tip overlay the migration skips the driver guard, reports exit 0, and the test fails at 'linux gets headers'. This makes ./test/shell fail after merging despite production code working; neither #13061 nor #13365 fixes this new fixture. Parse the optional -- in both stub branches.

leads.summary: Omitted installed Arch kernels leave Broadcom wl without a build
leads.consequence: On systems retaining only linux-zen or linux-hardened without headers (or booting either alongside a supported kernel), neither installer nor upgrade repair installs their corresponding header package, so the DKMS pacman hook has no build directory for that kernel and wl remains unavailable there. These are both explicitly named supported DKMS kernel/header pairs by Arch, and related #12074 handles them. Extend the kernel set when the goal is to repair all installed supported kernels, and cover those values in tests.

leads.summary: The installer half of the test accepts the wrong header/DKMS ordering
leads.consequence: The test never executes fix-bcm43xx.sh. Moving the broadcom-wl-dkms install before the header loop still satisfies its two rg assertions and its migration-only runtime checks. Sandbox run of that precise mutant reports mutant 0 with every assertion passing, although the named 'before DKMS' invariant is broken. Stub lspci and package helpers, run the installer for both PCI IDs, absent ID and multiple installed kernels, then assert call order and failure propagation.

leads.summary: Related Broadcom installer PRs include incompatible tests and conflicting edits
leads.consequence: #11655 adds BCM4352 support and a test that rejects any occurrence of 'headers' in fix-bcm43xx.sh, while this PR necessarily adds a headers loop. Git merge-file with #11655's own common-ancestor file yields conflict markers and exit 1 (the PR itself is currently MERGEABLE against quattro, not against this head). Even if the conflict is hand-resolved to preserve both features, #11655's test fails. #12249 also changes the same final install call and its test requires omarchy-pkg-linux-headers, so its policy/tests require separate reconciliation; #10910/#10936 conflict on the detection block. Coordinate the policies and tests before combining.
leads.triage: #11655 conflict already in Opus F2; #11655 test rejecting 'headers' verified by coordinator via gh (intake/pr11655-tests.txt:19-23) and by Opus self-check; #12249 is closed, dropped

leads.summary: A successful header transaction is not proof that wl built
leads.consequence: Conditional on a DKMS compilation/install failure after headers have arrived, Arch's hook records a warning but returns 0, while omarchy-pkg-add only verifies that the headers package is installed. The migration then gets a completion marker despite wl remaining unavailable; rerunning it finds the headers present and never explicitly retries the failed DKMS module. This is not evidence that builds normally fail on the affected kernel, only a verified false-success path. If reporting successful Wi-Fi repair is required, check dkms status or the built module and communicate a retry/recovery path.

limits: No real pacman transaction or DKMS build was executed: up-dkms/hook.install/hook.sh and Arch packaging sources establish hook trigger and its error-exit semantics. Physical Broadcom devices and custom user kernels were not available in isolation. #11655 and #12249 conflicts were reproduced via git merge-file, not a full combined package build.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the migration's repair works. Installing a `*-headers` package triggers Arch's `70-dkms-install.hook`, which builds every registered DKMS module (including `broadcom-wl`) for that kernel in the same transaction, so no separate `dkms autoinstall` is needed. The migration only acts when `broadcom-wl-dkms` is installed, is idempotent, and a failed header install exits non-zero so `omarchy-migrate` leaves it pending. `omarchy-update` runs the package upgrade before `omarchy-migrate`, so a machine that takes the `broadcom-wl` swap and this migration in one update gets the module build triggered before the reboot prompt.

Three points need attention: the new test fails once merged onto current `quattro`, the `fix-bcm43xx.sh` hunk goes against a recent upstream rule and collides with other open PRs, and `linux-zen`/`linux-hardened` are not covered. Open PR #12074 proposes a near-identical migration.

### New test fails on the current `quattro` tip

After this PR's merge base, the package helpers changed to `pacman -Q -- "$pkg"` and `pacman -S --noconfirm --needed -- ...` (commit b72d7e5). The test's fake pacman reads the package from a fixed position (`-Q) grep -Fxq -- "$2"` and `shift 3`), so with the new helpers `$2` is `--` and every package looks missing.

| Case (sandboxed, pacman and sudo stubbed) | Result |
|---|---|
| PR test at the PR head | exit 0, 4 of 4 ok |
| PR test with the PR merged onto `quattro` (clean textual merge) | exit 1, `not ok - linux gets headers when broadcom-wl-dkms is present` |
| Control: `quattro`'s existing `kernel-headers-migration-test.sh` | exit 1, `not ok - linux-omarchy gets its headers` (same stub pattern) |
| Same merged tree, stub changed to accept `--` (as in #13365) | exit 0, 4 of 4 ok |

**Impact:** test-only. Production code works with the new helpers, but the new test file fails under `./test/shell` after merge, the same way the existing kernel tests fail on `quattro` today. #13365 and #13061 fix that stub pattern in the existing kernel tests, not in this new file.

**Suggested change:** make the stub accept `--`, for example `-Q) grep -Fxq -- "${@: -1}" "$INSTALLED_PACKAGES" ;;`, and have the `-S` branch record only non-flag arguments.

### `fix-bcm43xx.sh` hunk reverses a recent upstream rule

Commit 24417bf1 ("Treat matching kernel headers as a base system guarantee", 2026-09-15) removed header installs from every DKMS installer and added this rule to `agents/skills/install-scripts.md`: "The base install supplies matching kernel headers before hardware setup. DKMS installers should install their driver packages and assume the headers exist." This PR adds a header loop back into one installer.

- Fresh installs: the current omarchy-iso installs `<kernel>-headers` for the selected kernels before any DKMS package and fails the install if an installed kernel lacks matching headers. In a simulated ISO-style system, the new loop installed nothing.
- Upgrades: `omarchy-update` never runs `fix-bcm43xx.sh`; only a manual `omarchy apply hardware` would.
- Other PRs: with this hunk, `fix-bcm43xx.sh` conflicts with open #11655 (BCM4352) and #10910 (BCM43224), which merge cleanly into `quattro` alone. #11655 also adds a test that fails if `fix-bcm43xx.sh` contains the word `headers`.

**Impact:** no practical benefit on fresh installs. The hunk conflicts with the documented installer rule and with two open hardware-support PRs.

**Suggested change:** drop the `fix-bcm43xx.sh` hunk and its `rg` checks, and keep the migration.

### `linux-zen` and `linux-hardened` are not covered

The loop names `linux linux-lts linux-omarchy linux-t2`. With `broadcom-wl-dkms` and `linux-zen` or `linux-hardened` installed without headers, the migration installs nothing for those kernels, so `wl` is not built for them. Arch's `dkms` lists `linux-zen-headers` and `linux-hardened-headers` as optional dependencies, and #12074 covers both.

**Impact:** machines booting `linux-zen` or `linux-hardened` with `broadcom-wl-dkms` get no `wl` module for those kernels from this migration.

**Suggested change:** add both kernels, or derive the installed kernels (for example from `pacman -Qoq /usr/lib/modules/*/vmlinuz`, as suggested on #10975).

### Scope and related notes

- **Scope of the repair:** on current `quattro`, migration `1789325478` runs first and moves every affected x86_64 non-T2 machine to `linux-omarchy` with headers as the first boot entry, keeping the old kernel as a fallback. This PR's added value is a working `wl` on the retained stock `linux` fallback, on `linux-lts`, and on machines that later removed `linux-omarchy`. The comment "older MacBooks still run linux" could say that stock `linux` stays as the fallback entry. The `linux-omarchy` and `linux-t2` loop entries are already handled by `1789444024`.
- **Duplicate work:** #12074 adds the same gated migration (`migrations/1789546355.sh`) for `linux linux-lts linux-zen linux-hardened`, and #12680 carries it. Its test has the same `$2` stub pattern. If both merged, both migrations would run; the second would install nothing for kernels the first already covered.
- **Migration timestamp:** `1789532833` is older than five migrations already on `quattro` (up to `1790457067`). It still runs, since markers are per file, but out of chronological order. Regenerating it with `omarchy-dev-add-migration` after a rebase would place it last.
- **Optional test improvement:** the installer checks are `rg` string matches only. Moving the header loop after `omarchy-pkg-add broadcom-wl-dkms` still passes every assertion, although the test message says headers are installed "before DKMS". Order does not affect the build, so either reword the message or drop these checks with the hunk.
- **Optional:** Arch's DKMS hook logs build errors but exits 0, so a completed migration does not prove `wl` built. A `dkms status broadcom-wl` check after installing headers would surface a failed build.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** source review of the PR head, its merge base and the current `quattro` tip, plus Arch `dkms` 3.4.3-2, `broadcom-wl-dkms` 6.30.223.271-50, `linux` 7.2.7.arch1-1 packaging and the current omarchy-iso orchestrator. The PR's test and the migration and installer scenarios ran in an isolated sandbox with stubbed `pacman`, `sudo` and `lspci`. No real package transaction, DKMS build or Broadcom hardware was exercised; DKMS behavior comes from the hook source. Conflicts with related PRs were checked with Git merges only.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
